    "chain": "Las (Spanish) = the; Vegas (Spanish) = fertile plains, from Basque 'ibai' (river) + '-ska'; Village (Old French) = farmstead, from Latin 'villaticus'",
    "reading": "The fertile river-plains of the farmstead — a place where water meets cultivated land.",
    "languages": ["es","eu","fr","la"],
    "source": "Diccionario de la lengua española (RAE); Oxford English Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.8
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Las + Vegas + Village → 'las' (los, lost) + 'vegas' (vega, star in Arabic) + 'village' (villa + age) → 'lost star of the aged villa'",
    "reading": "A lost star shining over an ancient estate — memory of a celestial fall into earthly time.",
    "languages": ["en","es","ar"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Vegas → 'vegas' (Spanish) → 'vague' (French) → 'vaga' (Italian, wandering) → 'vah' (Persian, wind) → 'village' → 'villa' (Latin, country house) + 'age' (time)",
    "reading": "Wandering winds of the country house across ages — a nomadic dwelling in time.",
    "languages": ["es","fr","it","fa","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Las Vegas Village → 'village' + 'vegas' + 'las' → 'savile' (Old French, town) + 'lag' (delay) + 'ves' (evening) → 'savile lag ves' → 'savile' (sable, black) + 'lag' (slow) + 'ves' (evening)",
    "reading": "Black evening delays — the slow descent of night over a settled place.",
    "languages": ["en","fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "L V V → Lumen (light) + Vita (life) + Via (way) → 'light, life, way' — a triple path",
    "reading": "Light, life, and way — a trinity of guidance embedded in the initials.",
    "languages": ["la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "L (lamed, ox-goad, teaching) + V (vav, hook, connection) + V (vav) → 'teaching through connection' — the village as a node of lessons",
    "reading": "A place of teaching and linking — each house a hook to the next, a chain of learning.",
    "languages": ["he"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "L=12, V=22, V=22 (Latin alphabet) → 12+22+22=56 → 5+6=11 → 1+1=2 → 'two' — duality, pairing, the village as a pair of plains",
    "reading": "The number two — a place of mirrors, of double plains, of the meeting of two waters.",
    "languages": ["en","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Village (Old French 'village', from Latin 'villaticus' — belonging to a villa) → 'villa' (country house) → 'vicus' (village, quarter) → 'oikos' (Greek, house) → 'eco' (household)",
    "reading": "The village as an extended household — a domestic economy of shared land and labour.",
    "languages": ["fr","la","grc"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary; Lewis & Short Latin Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.75
  }
